newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel snuffs out small platform fire.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel snuffs out small platform fire.

text.p: Eurotunnel Plc, still smarting from the effects of a major fire which swept in the Channel tunnel in November, reported another small fire had broken out on a platform at Folkestone inb southern England at 0543 GMT on Thursday but was soon snuffed out, with no casualties.

A spokeswoman for the trouble-prone tunnel told Reuters "There was a very small fire on the platform on the UK side of the tunnel. It was due to an electrical fault and lasted half an hour." No passengers were involved.
Kent Fire Brigade was called in to give the station the all-clear. The train at the platform concerned was a passenger shuttle, which was empty at the time.
This latest embarrassment follows another small fire, which broke out inside the tunnel in the aftermath of the main incident, which happened on November 18.
The Channel Tunnel Safety Authority is currently investigating the cause of the November 18 fire, which led to serious disruption of freight and passenger services.
Industry estimates put the cost of the fire, including repairs and compensation payouts at as much as 200 million pounds ($334.3 million). Eurotunnel has said it is fully insured.
